title: `in_` on nested `CompoundSelect` raises `NotImplementedError`

labels.name: great mcve
labels.description: An issue with a great mcve

body:
### Describe the bug

SQLAlchemy core fails to compile a statement which uses the `in_` operator on a nested `CompoundSelect` object, i.e. `INTERSECT` of `UNION`s or vice-versa. It does work if the inner `CompoundStatement` is not the first argument to the outer one, producing a valid SQL.



### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

2.0.44

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

n/a

### Database Vendor and Major Version

n/a

### Python Version

3.12

### Operating system

OSX

### To Reproduce

```python
from sqlalchemy import column, intersect, select, table, union

t = table("t", column("c1"), column("c2"))

def main() -> None:
    # It doesn't matter if union or intersect is used.
    inner_compound_stmt = union(
        select(t.c.c1).where(t.c.c2 == "x"),
        select(t.c.c1).where(t.c.c2 == "y"),
    )
    simple_stmt = select(t.c.c1).where(t.c.c2 == "z")

    # When simple statement is first, no issues.
    outer_compound_stmt = intersect(simple_stmt, inner_compound_stmt)
    stmt = select(t).where(t.c.c1.in_(outer_compound_stmt))
    print(stmt)

    # When compound statement is first, NotImplementedError is raised.
    outer_compound_stmt = intersect(inner_compound_stmt, simple_stmt)
    # Other selects don't matter, error is raised also when compound statement is alone.
    # outer_compound_stmt = intersect(inner_compound_stmt)
    select(t).where(t.c.c1.in_(outer_compound_stmt))  # raises NotImplementedError


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### Error

```
FROM t 
WHERE t.c1 IN (SELECT t.c1 
FROM t 
WHERE t.c2 = :c2_1 INTERSECT (SELECT t.c1 
FROM t 
WHERE t.c2 = :c2_2 UNION SELECT t.c1 
FROM t 
WHERE t.c2 = :c2_3))

``` 

### Additional context

I hit this issue in production where compound queries are built from user provided logic expressions transformed into CNF (conjunction of disjunctions, or in SQL terms `INTERSECT` of `UNION`s). Because the intermediate representation uses sets, which have undetermined ordering, the queries would fail randomly, only when the first argument for `intersect` happened to be a `CompoundSelect` produced by the `union` function.
